strategies.name: support_to_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, identify intraday support on the 5-minute chart using price action and/or moving averages acting as support, then enter when price comes down to that support and bounces. Exit the scalp into the next resistance area rather than holding for a larger move.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly at resistance or after the short upward move; do not overstay the trade. Risk/management is framed as small, fast in-and-out trades with immediate profit-taking once the bounce plays out.

variants.timeframe_note: 5-minute chart after allowing first 5 to 15 minutes to establish support
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter when price tags the 13 EMA acting as support and bounces
variants.target_note: exit into the quick move/resistance; small scalp profit
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support... the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter off deeper support at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA no longer holds support
variants.target_note: ride from support to resistance and exit quickly
variants.transcript_quote: another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status

strategies.name: support_breakdown_short_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: Once a key support level is lost, enter in the direction of the breakdown to catch the fast move lower. This is taught as the bigger scalp that comes after repeated support bounces fail.
strategies.exit_summary: Cover/take profit quickly after the sharp downward move rather than holding indefinitely. Management remains the same scalp style: get in, take the move, and get out fast.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter after price loses the 200 EMA support
variants.target_note: exit after the large flush lower
variants.transcript_quote: once we lost the support of the 200 look at this move boom boom boom you want to exit right there okay that's your big scout you would have entered

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches two distinct executable skeletons: a long support-bounce scalp into resistance, and the opposite-direction short scalp after support breaks; repeated examples off 13 EMA vs 200 EMA are variants of the same support-bounce idea.
